KEY AUDIT MATTER:
Provisions for claims and other liabilities
The estimation of the Group’s provisions for claims and other
liabilities involves high levels of judgement. There is uncertainty
as to how claims will be resolved and therefore significant
judgement is required in assessing the likely outcome and
the potential liability for such matters. Matters that impact
judgement include the nature of the claim, specific facts and
circumstances of the claim and the impact of decided cases on
the existing open cases and claims.
Refer to note 3 (i) on critical accounting estimates and
assumptions and note 25 on provision for claims and other
liabilities.
HOW OUR AUDIT ADDRESSED THE KEY AUDIT MA:
Our procedures in relation to adequacy of the provision for claims
and other liabilities included:
• evaluating and testing management’s controls over
provisioning;
• comparing actual amounts paid during the year to
provision amounts held in the prior periods, to evaluate the
reasonableness of management’s estimation process;
• assessing the reasonability and sufficiency of the provision
for claims and other liabilities by challenging judgements
taken by management in determining amounts to be
provided for; and,
• checking the completeness of the register of claims and
other liabilities against confirmations received from the
Group’s external legal counsel.
